attempts.approach: Imports SM.SoftRotation, SM.Admissible, SM.Fibres. def:anchors is encoded as a common data structure SoftAnchorData (parent, insertion vertex, vector, the lem:soft-generic bound ε₀ with its generic-and-one-chamber specification, and the parameter 0 < ε < ε₀), three extensions ZeroAnchor / LoopAnchor / LoopAnchorZero carrying the case-specific conditions (parent rotation, parent turn, sector), and an inductive Anchor m r whose three constructors carry the printed case hypotheses (Z) Admissible (n-1) r, (L) MinimalAdmissible n r ∧ |r| ≥ 2, (L₀) (n,r) = (4,0). Genericity of anchors comes from bound_spec; rotation comes from SM.soft_rotation_of_regular_interval applied on the whole interval (0, ε₀) (regularity from genericity), giving rot = rot P in the mixed sector and rot P - τ_j in the loop sector; for (L) this is (r - sgn r) - (-sgn r) = r, for (L₀) rotationNumber_triangle gives rot P = τ_j so the result is 0. Sector nonemptiness: the loop sector is openCone (-u) (-v) and the open cone openCone u (-v) lies in the mixed sector (SM.soft_loop_sector_iff, determinant sign computation); along the ray u' + b v' (b > 0) each condition det(q, μ_k - μ_j) = 0 has at most one root (Cramer: u', v' independent and μ_k ≠ μ_j by G1 injectivity), so finitely many b are excluded and Set.Ioi_infinite.exists_notMem_finite picks an admissible q; det(u,q), det(q,v) ≠ 0 follow from the cone formulas. Exhaustion/disjointness is integer arithmetic (omega after abs_cases). (Z) existence: generic (n-1)-gon of rotation r from SM.exists_generic_of_admissible (lem:fibres), any vertex, mixed q, δ from SM.soft_family_regular_data, ε = δ/2. (L₀): a generic triangle from lem:fibres with (3,1) admissible, loop insertion at vertex 0. (L): from minimality n - 1 = 2|r| and r ≠ 0; a generic (2|r|-1)-gon of rotation r - sgn r exists by lem:fibres ((2|r|-1, r - sgn r) is admissible); a mixed-sector soft insertion at vertex 0 keeps the rotation and, by lem:soft-generic (ii) (SM.softInsertion_attachment_turns), creates corners with turns -χ_-, -χ_+ which are opposite nonzero signs, so one equals -sgn r; a loop-sector insertion at that corner is the loop anchor. Both signs of r are handled directly (no reflection needed).
attempts.obstacles: omega treats |r| as an atom, so all abs reasoning is done after abs_cases / abs_of_neg etc. Structure-instance continuation lines must be indented past the opening brace (otherwise 'expected }'). Decidability of ∀ over SignType with ≠ hypotheses fails, so the sign case lemmas use revert + cases + decide. Dependent rewriting of r in Anchor.polygon_rotation requires subst rather than rw. The SignType-to-ℝ casts are not handled by push_cast alone; SignType.coe_one / coe_neg_one are rewritten first. No mathematical obstacles remained; the (L) existence was obtained by a construction different from the printed one (see fidelity_notes).
attempts.fidelity_notes: (1) Vertex counts: the source's admissible pair (n, r) ∈ ℤ × ℤ is rendered as ((m : ℤ) + 1, r) where m : ℕ [NeZero m] is the parent's vertex count, so an anchor is literally an (m+1)-gon LabelledTuple (m+1) = P^{(j,q)}_ε = softInsertion P j q ε, the parent an m-gon; 'n ≥ 4' is 4 ≤ (m:ℤ)+1 (equivalently 3 ≤ m, stored as parent_card). The exhaustion clause is stated for integer pairs (n r : ℤ) exactly as printed. (2) Labels in ZMod: the old vertex μ_k is at label softOldIndex j k, the new vertex μ_* at softNewIndex j = softOldIndex j j + 1; the soft edge E_j 'from μ_j to μ_* = μ_{j+1} in the labelling of the anchor' is the edge at label softOldIndex j j (SoftAnchorData.softEdge), and softEdge_spec proves it runs from P j to P j + ε q with edge vector ε q. (3) ε₀ = ε₀(P, j, q) 'the bound of lem:soft-generic' is carried as data (field bound) with the specification 'on (0, ε₀) the insertion is generic and lies in one chamber' taken from SM.soft_family_regular_data: existence of a base B : GenericTuple (m+1) with every P_ε (0 < ε < ε₀) generic, in labelledChamber B and with projection in chamber (polygonProjection B). The existential over B is inside the field (bound_spec), so the bound is 'part of the anchor data' and not uniform over anything else. Genericity/one-chamber for the anchors is thus by construction; rotation is derived from lem:soft-rotation on that interval. (4) Sectors are the printed sign conditions of lem:soft-generic (iv): mixed χ_- ≠ χ_+, loop χ_- = χ_+ = τ_j, with χ_± = softAttachmentMinus/Plus and τ_j = turn P j; sgn r = SignType.sign r cast to ℝ or negated in SignType. (5) Cases: the Anchor inductive requires the case hypothesis as printed in each constructor ((Z) Admissible (n-1) r; (L) MinimalAdmissible n r ∧ 2 ≤ |r|; (L₀) (n, r) = (4, 0)); the standing hypothesis 'admissible with n ≥ 4' is not repeated as a separate parameter because each case hypothesis implies it. LoopAnchorZero records 'P is a triangle' as the field triangle : m = 3. (6) 'Exactly one applies' is stated as the disjunction plus the three pairwise exclusions. (7) 'Has n vertices' is the type LabelledTuple (m+1) of Anchor.polygon. (8) Construction for (L): instead of the printed midpoint subdivision of K_{r-1}, displacement to create a right turn, perturbation to generic and reflection for r ≤ -2, the parent is obtained as follows: a generic (2|r|-1)-gon of rotation r - sgn r exists by lem:fibres (SM.exists_generic_of_admissible), and a mixed-sector soft insertion (lem:soft-generic (i),(ii), lem:soft-rotation) yields a generic 2|r|-gon of rotation r - sgn r whose two new corners have turns -χ_- and -χ_+ of opposite signs, one of which is -sgn r; the loop anchor is a loop-sector insertion there. This is a valid alternative construction (permitted by the task) and it handles r ≥ 2 and r ≤ -2 uniformly; the stars K_{r-1} and the reflection are not used. The sector-nonemptiness proof follows the printed argument (open cones, finitely many excluded lines) but exhibits the mixed vectors via the sub-cone strictly between ℓ_{j-1} and -ℓ_j rather than the whole complement. (9) The (L₀) triangle is any generic triangle (one exists by lem:fibres with (3,1)); the printed 'counterclockwise triangle' is not needed since rotationNumber_triangle gives rot P = τ_j for either orientation, and the clause 'for a triangle P and any of its vertices j' is proved for every generic triangle and vertex (loopAnchorZero_of_parent). (10) Additional prescribability clauses (parent/vertex prescribed in (L₀), and in (L) given a parent with the printed properties) are proved as extra conjuncts beyond the printed statement.

attempts.approach: Imports SM.TreeReversal (for IntervalComposition.ext', parts_le_leaves, sum_part_leaves), SM.UnaryComposition (eq_single_of_parts_eq_one, single_product) and SM.BowTie (bowTie, bowTie_G1). General machinery: (a) the k-th cut of a composition satisfies left+k ≤ cut k and cut k + (parts-k) ≤ right (induction on k using StrictMono), hence a composition with parts = leaves cuts at every boundary vertex and is unique (via ext'); (b) every two-leaf open sum vanishes (openTreeSum_many + parts_le_leaves forces parts = 2 + binary_ordinaryWeight_zero); (c) the product of open sums over an all-leaves composition is 1; (d) rootWeight of a two-part composition equals its single near sign (rootGate d d = d, via binary_near_eq_far), and root/ordinary weights of three-part compositions are the product of two gates (Fintype.prod_eq_mul). Clause (i): the triangle's full interval [0,2] has exactly two compositions (single, triangleBinaryComposition); Fintype.sum_eq_single on the binary one (the single term is 1·b_[0,2] = 0) gives A_g = χ(g, g+2, g+1) = χ(a_2,a_1,a_0); turns are cyclic permutations of one triple (chi_cyclic, explicit ZMod 3 case split), τ = turn P 0 ≠ 0 by G1, and χ(g,g+2,g+1) = -τ_{g+1} = -τ by chi_swap_last. Clause (ii): for any (G1) quadrilateral, compositions of [0,3] are single / two-part / quadTernaryComposition; two-part terms vanish because a child has two leaves (sum_part_leaves + Fintype.sum_eq_add); Fintype.sum_eq_add on single and ternary gives A_g = V⁻(ternary) − V⁺(ternary); the four near/far signs are identified with d₁,h₁,d₂,h₂ (simp on boundaryIndex, push_cast, ring1/linear_combination with (4 : ZMod 4) = 0); an 81-case SignType case split (norm_num [rootGate, ordinaryGate, signTheta]) yields eq:root-bowtie-recursion and (d₁h₂+h₁d₂)/2. For bowTie the 16 chirotope values at the four roots are computed from the coordinates (sign_eq_(neg_)one_iff + simp +decide [bowTie, det]) reproducing the printed table, each row giving -1; shifts are handled by treeCoefficient_shift (with g+k−k = g), and an integer-k version plus (shift 1)^[k] = shift k are added.
attempts.obstacles: Minor only: (1) `ring` does not fail when it cannot close a goal (it falls back to ring_nf), so inside `first | … | linear_combination h4` one must use `ring1`. (2) `simp only` left Nat casts like ↑(1+2) unreduced; solved with the Nat.reduceAdd/Nat.reduceSub simprocs plus push_cast. (3) `show i = 0 ∨ i = 1 ∨ i = 2 by decide` needs `decide +revert` for a free ZMod variable. (4) Products over Fin (π.parts − 1) with a hypothesis π.parts = 2 or 3 cannot be rewritten to Fin 1 / Fin 2 directly; handled with Finset.prod_eq_single / Fintype.prod_eq_mul on explicit indices. No mathematical obstacles; nothing remains unproved.
attempts.fidelity_notes: Labels live in ZMod n with the source label n ≡ 0 (bow-tie label 4 is 0 : ZMod 4, matching BowTie.lean). Physical root g ∈ ZMod n; the boundary word at root g is a_i = P (g + i + 1) (boundaryIndex), so for n = 4: a_0 = P(g+1), a_1 = P(g+2), a_2 = P(g+3), a_3 = P(g+4) = P g; the source's d₁ = χ(a_2,a_1,a_0), d₂ = χ(a_3,a_2,a_1), h₁ = χ(a_3,a_1,a_0), h₂ = χ(a_3,a_2,a_0) are stated as chi P (g+3) (g+2) (g+1), chi P g (g+3) (g+2), chi P g (g+2) (g+1), chi P g (g+3) (g+1). Clause (i) is stated exactly as requested: ∀ P : LabelledTuple 3, ∀ hP : G1 P, ∃ τ : SignType, τ ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ i, turn P i = τ) ∧ ∀ g, treeCoefficient P hP g (by norm_num) = -(τ : ℤ); the sign τ is a SignType cast to ℤ. Clause (ii): ∀ k g : ZMod 4, treeCoefficient (shift k bowTie) (g1_shift_forward k bowTie_G1) g (by norm_num) = -1, where shift 1 is the source σ (Polygon.lean) and σ^k = shift k; the source's "every integer k" is covered by A_small_values_ii_int (k : ℤ cast to ZMod 4) and smallValues_shift_iterate ((shift 1)^[k] P = shift (k : ZMod n) P). The G1 proof for shift k bowTie is g1_shift_forward k bowTie_G1 (bowTie_G1 = bowTie_generic.1 = star_generic_iv.1.1); by proof irrelevance any other G1 proof gives the same term. eq:root-bowtie-recursion is proved for every (G1) quadrilateral (quad_treeCoefficient) with exact ℤ-division by 4 and by 2 (numerators lie in {-4,0,4} resp. {-2,0,2}); the printed sign table appears as the sixteen chi evaluations in bowTie_treeCoefficient (rows in the order g = 4≡0, 1, 2, 3, each commented with (d₁,d₂,h₁,h₂)). (5) A regular closed polygon's edges lie in no closed semicircle (source argument: nonnegative dots summing to zero vanish, all edges on the line v⊥ with coefficients det v e_i, adjacent coefficients have equal sign by regularity, cyclic induction, sum ≠ 0). (6) Nonzero rotation: linear interpolation of lifts; steps stay < π (convex combination lemma); closed-semicircle containment would put the Fin (n+1) lifted sequence in an interval of length π by SM.transport_angle_interval, giving 2π|r| ≤ π, impossible for r ≠ 0. (7) Zero rotation: convex charts 𝓐(h,d) in ZMod n → ℝ; chart points have no closed semicircle (transport_angle_interval on the sequence θ_{h+j}); charts cover (max/min argument, d ∉ {0,1,n−1} by the step bound); explicit plateau witnesses (3π/2 / 3π/4 / 0 profile, so every step is 0 or ±3π/4) realise both moves of transport:chart-moves for 2 ≤ d ≤ n−3; descending d to 2 and advancing h by 𝓐(h,2)→𝓐(h,3)→𝓐(h+1,2) (Nat.le_induction / induction on k with k = (−h).val) joins every chart point to a base point, giving JoinedIn/IsPathConnected of the union for n ≥ 5; a Path in the union (via Set.projIcc) is fed to mycyc_reconstruct_angles.
